newsitem.title: DUBAI: Qatar Airways plans bigger cargo share of revenue.
newsitem.headline: Qatar Airways plans bigger cargo share of revenue.

text.p: Qatar Airways said on Tuesday it would work to increase air freight's contribution to overall revenues and that it planned to take over the operation of the Doha airport cargo terminal early next year.
"We are placing a major emphasis on cargo because for many airlines it is the profit stream," the airline's senior general manager Michael Hewitt told a news briefing in Dubai.
"By early next year we will be operating the cargo terminal at Doha airport. The terminal needs extensive work and we plan to do this, including putting in place proper racks," he said.
Hewitt said cargo's contribution to total revenue in the past year was around seven percent. "But we think that will grow to 12 percent this year."
The three-year-old airline has a fleet of eight aircraft. The six in scheduled operation include four Boeing 727s and two leased Airbus A300-600s. Two Boeing 747s are to be used for charters.
Hewitt said the airline had no plans to buy freighters.

Qatar Airways is 70 percent owned by the Qatar ruling family. Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani is the chairman of the board. Qatari individuals and institutions own the rest.
